families.scaffolding_and_connected_parts: Multiple representations remain parts of the same source comparison.

families.answer_form: Validity verdict and its evidence.
families.difficulty_progression: YMExample1/Try1 juxtapose graphs,tables and lists,including harmless repeated outputs.
families.distinction_basis: Function validity is distinct from injectivity and from calculating a value.

insights.title: Function meaning,domains and images
insights.teaching_comparison: YM compares graphs,tables,lists and mappings before notation,domain/image projections and formula-derived ranges. It explicitly separates function validity from one-to-one status. Its range progression moves from monotone affine functions to restricted quadratics with interior extrema and open endpoints. Goldie2&3uses functions and polynomial graphs as assumed background rather than providing a parallel introductory sequence;its retained algebra sketches cannot replace these definition/domain tasks.
insights.examination_comparison: NSSCAS2022P1Q6(a)asks a logarithm domain;2023P1Q2(b)asks an inverse domain;2025P1Q7(c)asks a restricted quadratic range. YM supplies useful lower scaffolds in relation validity and graph projections,but those do not cover all of the formula/branch reasoning. A pointwise product is not composition even if printed letters are adjacent. ERR04supports the importance of domain/inverse/graph links,not an error count for every textbook relation task.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: E03sets terminology and simple injectivity/inverses;C03/A03include domain/range identification and linked function work. Increased demand comes from endpoint attainment,interior extrema and propagated exclusions,not coefficient size. Full-circle relation projection is supporting representation practice,not a function on the whole circle.
insights.pitfalls: YMExample12prints a wrong pole sign and an impossible negative part of a root-function image;Example4has a sign typo in an intermediate header. Repeated outputs do not violate function validity;conflicting outputs for one input do. Distinguish textbook/source defects from examiner-confirmed learner confusion;ERR04is only broad corroboration for the linked domain issue.
insights.gaps_and_representations: YM provides explicit multi-representation function definitions lacking in the retained Goldieprogression. A given graph and a worked solution graph have different roles;domain/range can be read from the former but must be derived from a formula in another family. A flag for graph use does not prove that the learner must draw it.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose separate response checks for relation validity,injectivity,input set and attained image. Carry endpoint inclusions and poles through every connected stage. Preserve table/list and graphical representations as branches instead of converting all tasks into equations.

insights.title: Injectivity,restricted inverse rules and branch resets
insights.teaching_comparison: YM moves from inverse algebra to reflection and then a quadratic branch restriction. It distinguishes a least right-hand endpoint from a greatest left-hand endpoint,and later resets a parameter for a new inverse. Its piecewise example maps each output interval to a separate inverse clause. Goldieassumes inverse/function background in its logarithm/trigonometry chapters;those later special-function methods broaden instances but do not supply a substitute forYM’s explicit branch-selection sequence.
insights.examination_comparison: NSSCAS2023P1Q2(a)(b)separates inverse expression/domain;2025P1Q7(b)(c)(d)links one-to-one restriction,range and inverse. YM13/Try13andExercise3.1Q3closely support that reasoning. Source branch resets such asm=5after choosing leastm=3must survive;borrowing a sign/domain from an earlier answer changes the task. ERR04confirms that linked domain/inverse reasoning matters.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: E03includes simple inverse decisions;C03/A03permit linked branch/domain work. A restricted quadratic needs a sign decision justified by the original domain. Piecewise inverse intervals and parameter-dependent ranges are harder through logical conditions rather than larger constants. QUAL08requires preserving the branch actually used.
insights.pitfalls: YMExample10asks an inverse at-2although its inverse input must be nonnegative;Try10Q2(c)omits the original quadratic branch. These are registered source defects. A formally rearranged squared expression is not a valid inverse everywhere. Try13Q2also illustrates why a later explicit reset must override the preliminary extremal bound.
insights.gaps_and_representations: YM provides abundant quadratic restrictions and some piecewise practice. The sampled exams include rational and logarithmic inverse forms as well;later special-function chapters must supply that breadth. A textbook error is retained as internal caution,not an approved defective learner prompt.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose a persistent original-domain→image→inverse-domain ledger and a source-part parameter state. Test both inverse compositions only on their admitted sets. Keep valid alternate inverse forms while requiring the correct branch and endpoint strictness.

insights.title: Composition order,decomposition and whole-domain admissibility
insights.teaching_comparison: YM explicitly teaches pointwise operations before ordered composition,evaluation before symbolic formation,and then equations,missing rules and full-domain containment. Try9Q5uses commuting inverse affine rules as a counterexample to an unqualified never-commutes claim. Try14Q3asks why one order fails on a declared domain even though the algebraic expression exists for some inputs. Goldie’s later chained standard functions give context for these methods,but its retained corpus lacks the same introductory decomposition sequence.
insights.examination_comparison: NSSCAS2023P1Q2(c)(i)(ii)asks a composite rule then a parameter condition at one input. That observed chain does not alone cover recognising a missing component or checking the whole inner image against the outer domain. YM14/Try14andExercise3.1Q4add positivity,strict domains and correlated parameters. Textbook-derived inverse/composite proofs must not be presented as official marking criteria.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: C03/A03explicitly include forming composites and recognising decomposition. The structural increase is from evaluating a supplied pair to recovering an unknown rule or proving image containment. A reciprocal pole and a branch reset can matter even when symbolic expressions simplify to polynomials.
insights.pitfalls: YMExample7has a wrong nested-function step beside correct numeric outputs;Try14Q1’s inverse domain isSTRICTx>10. Revision3Q2(c)includes degeneratek=0in its no-solution set. A discriminant-only author solution can miss the degree-losing case. These are individually checked source/author cautions;no specific examiner-frequency claim is inferred.
insights.gaps_and_representations: The books/exams emphasise different directions:known-rule substitution is common,missing-rule and whole-domain admissibility are extraYMbreadth. Multiplying outputs is a different operation. One valid sample input does not establish a composition on the complete declared domain.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose separate fields for rule formation,point evaluation,missing-component recovery and whole-domain admissibility. Retain inner/outer identity and original poles even after simplification. Test degenerate parameter values before root-count theorems.

insights.title: Specified-domain sketches,inverse overlays and transformation investigations
insights.teaching_comparison: YM contrasts an asked original sketch,an inverse overlay on a supplied graph and a shared function/inverse diagram. Its six transformation investigations explicitly compare input/output shifts,reflections and reciprocal horizontal scales,including square-root domain changes. Goldie’s retained polynomial sketches provide end-behaviour/crossing practice,but not the same systematic inverse-reflection introduction. Later exponential/trigonometric chapters add special-function graph forms.
insights.examination_comparison: NSSCAS2022P1Q6(c)asks a logarithm/exponential inverse pair with intercepts;YM11’s affine pair supports reflection but lacks those asymptotes. YM13has a restricted quadratic and guidey=x;Example15asks an overlay on a GIVENpiecewise graph. They cannot all be collapsed into one generic drawing or an equation-only substitute.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: C03/A03name specified-domain original and inverse graphs. Difficulty grows through branch endpoints,asymptotes,piecewise images and coupled transformations. An extra guide line is a representation aid,not necessarily an additional assessed function. This synthesis proposes feature categories only;branch sketch marking is step3.
insights.pitfalls: Horizontal input shifts have opposite coordinate direction and horizontal scales are reciprocal. Those are textbook-derived teaching cautions. ERR04supports the general inverse/domain/graph link,but does not establish how frequently each transformation mistake occurs. The full graph must agree with its stated interval,including endpoint markers.
insights.gaps_and_representations: YM has structured transformations and affine/restricted quadratic inverse pairs;the exam’s logarithm asymptote requires additional sources later in thebook. Given image,worked solution image and requested learner image are separately recorded. No app capability hold is introduced:the owner’s diagram/sketch support decision remains binding.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose building all original,inverse and guide assets from shared function/domain data;preserve whether the learner draws anew or overlays. Keep explanation requirements in investigations rather than marking only plotted points. Bring exact feature/branch criteria to step3after source acceptance.

insights.title: Translate geometric graph constraints into equations
insights.teaching_comparison: YM teaches line/perpendicular midpoint constructions,then shape recovery,distance/gradient parameters,reflection and linked area/ratio tasks. Some diagrams provide data;others illustrate the worked solution. Goldie’s vectors chapter develops displacement and scalar-product geometry as a different method family;its retained graphs can support coordinate reasoning without replacing the explicit line-equation tasks inYM.
insights.examination_comparison: NSSCAS2024P1Q8asks oblique reflection by calculation;2025P1Q12asks a rhombus diagonal and vertices. YM20/Exercise3.2Q4/Try21Q2supply related geometry with varying scaffolds. A textbook’s step-by-step projection chain is easier guidance than the exam’s unscaffolded reflection even when the final calculation is similar. The2025diagram crop repair preserves allvertices andaxes;it is not authority to infer extra shape givens.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: E04andA04both connect graphs with equations;their broad statement does not prescribe numeric coordinate ranges. Difficulty varies by whether the crucial line/property is supplied or inferred,and by whether two valid parameter positions must be retained. These tasks also use explicit prior coordinate-geometry components;do not claim every distance calculation is a newASdemand.
insights.pitfalls: YMExercise3.2Q3has a vertical-gradient exception;Try19Q1/Q2have two correlated point branches;Revision3Q3expressly requests3dpinstead of the usual3sf. Example24only gives one diagonal bisection plus perpendicularity,so inventing a rhombus changes its constraints. These are source/author cautions;no dedicated examiner-error rate for them is claimed.
insights.gaps_and_representations: YM provides many shape/line chains;Goldie supplies alternative vector methods elsewhere. Supplied two-line intersection is less than inferring the lines from a diagram. An area or ratio final output requires evidence beyond a correct missing vertex. Both books’ conventions remain subordinate to the original question and official awards.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose preserving incidence,perpendicularity,midpoint and ordered-vertex constraints as explicit diagram invariants. Use independently computed coordinates and distances to check all labels. Retain scaffolded and unscaffolded reflection branches,axis-aligned exceptions and correlated alternatives.

insights.title: Graph intersections,tangency and parameter degeneration
insights.teaching_comparison: YM C1introduces substitution for numeric intersections and discriminant contact conditions;C3Example22adds a given intersection root,other-root recovery,tangency parameter and contact point. Try22uses a reciprocal curve,no-intersection interval,then actual intersections and their bisector. Goldie’s later tangent calculus provides another route in its proper context,but it does not make derivative calculation mandatory in an algebraic repeated-root task.
insights.examination_comparison: NSSCAS2022P1Q7and2021P1Q10(a)anchor line/curve intersection decisions. Supporting numeric systems omit some geometric interpretation;parameter tasks add repeated-root/no-root reasoning. The cited textbook chain adds a perpendicular bisector after recovering points,so it is broader than a short exam intersection part. A degree-losing single intersection is not automatically tangency.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: E04/C04explicitly connect intersections to equations and simple tangency to repeated roots. Harder cases are original poles,nonintersection intervals,linear degeneration and further geometric reuse. Larger coordinates alone do not boundgrade. GradeA04supports graph/equation relationships without importing unrestricted conic intersections.
insights.pitfalls: Original denominators remain excluded after clearing them. The geometric meaning of discriminantzero requires a genuine quadratic intersection equation;ERR05corroborates the danger of blindly applying discriminants outside that condition. A complete point requires recovering both coordinates,not just roots inx.
insights.gaps_and_representations: YM supplies numerical,parameter,contact-point and later-bisector branches;Goldie’s calculus context supplies a different method emphasis later. A topic tag does not make every intersection equally scaffolded. Root-count proofs and domain restrictions must stay explicit across the chain.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose independent original-equation substitution for all recovered points,explicit degree checks before discriminants,and graph labels generated from the same intersection solution. Preserve whether the source asks abscissas,whole points,contact or subsequent geometry.
